questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was still through my home university i just putted my wished, and the uni gave my an option to accept or declined the one they sent

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: As long as it's close to the university that would be perfect! Cause you gonna spend a lot of time around the school area, and your friends would also hang out around it, because of the different events that the school has. In my case the libraries where also close, so it was perfect. I lived in St. Vincent in sheffield, and loved the place because it was 10 min walk to the city and 10 min walk to the uni and libraries. But I had a lot of problems with the internet there so. bought my own and used that, but the accommodation payed for the internet that I bought.

Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was bit difficult cause i couldn't find how the exams where, but with writing to the host university they where really helpfull and wanted to help

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: After I got my approvel letter to start at University of Sheffield, I needed to choose which modules I wanted. I got accepted on all my modules, but when I went there I changed one of my modules to another one. Otherwise I would say I stressed for no reasons, and wanna say that, everything will be figures out anyway.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There was a dyslexia departement that was really help full, and the teachers are really helpfull as well.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes that I wished for before arriving there, but I changed one of them when I was there. And it wasn't a problem

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Don't stress. Everything will be figured out before and during your exchange. And if KU offeres you to get in contact with any other students from your home uni that's going on the exchange also, have them in your proces, cause sometime I couldn't find the things I needed with the registration, and it was nice to have someone that was in the same proces - as a sparring partner.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
I was satisfied with the programs, I choose 
International Humanitarian Law: it was a really interesting class, I didn't have any classes like that at KU, it was about armed conflict and what obligations does high contracting parties, civilians, commanders, and the military in general. 
Issues in comparative penology: was interesting in the fact of what harm/what we can learn from other countries, and not only England, but also in generel Europe.
Responding crime in Europe: was alright some of the last 3 classes listed here where bit the same, and not. They where under the same program Criminology program. 
And lastly Culture of Criminology: there where some of the things that where the same as the class "why punishment" at KU, but it had a lot more deepth in the theories, but also another approach. 
In general  liked the classes, but  also missed a litlle more "law".

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I had LLM classes, in England the master degrees are only for one year, and therefore the classes ometimes also talkes about there dissertation.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was kind of the same, there where mostly seminars, and I had some classes wheree there was a lecture on the scheme, but the classes where so small so it was like a seminar anyway. I think in general it was kind of the same as UCPH

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I travel more than I thought I would. It was a must to travel around UK, and the School makes some of the trips really cheap, but You need to be fast cause they will be sold out fast. So we made some trips me and my flatmates on our own. So we went to Liverpool, Manchester, Leeds, Birmingham, York, Oxford, London, Glasgow, Edinburg, Dublin etc, And I also travel to France and Spain. Sheffield is cheap, and I could have lower expenses, but it is a life experiences, so don't wanted to holdd back. But we cocked a lot home also.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food in general. if you go to stores such as Aldi and Lidl, it is so mcuh cheaper than Denmark. Veggies where cheaper. But also candy and ben&jerry.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There were so many opportunities. But I didn't go to any of them, but went to swim in my own, outside the school sports clubs. But there is many unions that many of my friends  choose, such as pole dancing, yoga, basket etc.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There where many language/cultur societies, and also a lot of sports.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: In general I had an amazing flat, so we did a lot of things together, in our own, but diffenately travel around, it was such an amazing way of seeing different cities, hearing different accents. People are so nice and try to make friends outside your own comfort. In our flat there where 3 sweds and 1 norwegian, and they talked the scandinavian language to each other, and I told them that I would appriciate if we talked english, cause I wanted to improve my English. And they respected that, but they still talked in their own language among each other, which made some of the others be little frustrated cause they wanted to be part of the conversations. So be carefull with finding people that speaks the same language, cause it is ofcourse more convient to speak your own language, but you also wanna learn. We made a group for our class, and I meet a lot of my classmates outside the school that way, and got a bigger networking that way. And in general be more curious about other peoples languages/cultures. It has been the most amazing thing to try being on exchange. And remember to be open about other peoples culture/opinions because and try to understand and engage in conversation about others. I have learned so much about so many other different cultures than the English one. So in general be curious, and try to get out of your comfort zone.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Like a said above, travel, try new things, ask people out i git invited to one of my classmates Chinese New Year, although he didn't invite the whole class, it was stilll an experience. And try to do somethings you haven't done, be openminded.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It wa quite easy. In the beginning it was bit difficult to understand central-Northern british accent, but a long a you just ask polite if they can speak slower mot people will try to speak so you understand. And please ask as many times as you can if you don't understand cause otherwise you wouldn't learn. The teachers are also aware of the amount of exchange students, so just remind them some times of they speak fast or you don't understand them.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I found it bit difficult socialising with the local students. But we made a whatsapp group (get used to it, they use WhatsApp a lot), and we went out 3 times, and from there it was easier to socializ. But it is bit difficult because they have their own friends and families around. So it is more typical to socialise with exchange students.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I didn't find any cultural differences particularly challenging, they are really polite, and I really liked that. But there are strikes all the time, and that was bit of a challenge, because some our classes got canceled. Trains got canceled often. So it could be expensive sometimes to take the uber

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I loved they are so polite, everyone is up for a chat. They are in general interested to hear about your and your culture. But they also don't mind explaining about their own culture.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Remember to be openminded, and ask as much as you can about anything, the teachers are really kind, and wants to help you if they can. 
2. if you are dislexes the papers that you submit shows that you have dyslexia, so that is not a problem at all. We could diffenitelly learn from that in UCPH. 
3. Enjoy the possibilities that is offered. Go in trips, try new things, and speak english as much as you can.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't be afraid of the exchange. The times flies away so fast. Speak english as much as you can, eventhough you're unsure about the accent/pronounce, because there is so many other students that also don't speak english as their first language. I didn't get good grades in english in high school, but I learned so much in these almost 5 months.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I have friends and network around the world, I have improved my english skills, I have learned to experience things in a different way. I'm so independent now, much more than I was before going, and I have had a lot of self-growth.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The beginning of the exchange where everything was new, and I didn't know how the exchange would be. But you get used to talking english everyday all day really fast, and you will settle down really fast also. Remeber that 5 months goes fast!

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: I would recommend everyone that has the possibility to do it! Go on exchange! it has been the best. Don't be afraid, but be curious! you will learn so much

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
